title: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter
summary: He considers no one played the blues like Kelly, who used plumber's-plunger and derby mutes and drew crowds to fights; also Pork Chop Rag and High Society.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: That's right, in the stand. He was a real blues man who really could mix him up. But there's none beat Chris Kelly. You like Chris Kelly. He was great. I wish they had some record of him. Yes, too bad. Yeah, he- I don't think it's another man born that may have it, could play the blues like him. Chris- uh, Callie's love, Chris Kelly, could have been the composer of it. It was so great. He really was great. And he would use so much in his trumpet, could do so much with it. And he had a toilet flusher, he'd use it, put a mute in it, then he'd put that down, he'd get his durb, he'd put it in, then he'd use the rim of his durb, he was really great. And he'd go take it, put it up against the wall, and get different tones of it. Oh, I mean he was great, he was really great. A blues man he was. He would make everybody get happy.
Happy until they fight, when he played the blues. That's actually the facts.
That's actually the fact. They would start the fight. Uh, he had the blues like we played, and B-flat blues we played and make that stop.
Yeah, the holler blues they got off that. Yeah, the holler blues they got off that.
I mean when he played that, they would start the fight.
And Pork Chop Rag, he was real great on that. High Society, ice cream, he really can play those numbers. He played ice cream too?
Oh yeah, all those numbers, yeah. I never heard anybody do that until about 1945, when once Jim Robinson and George Lewis. Oh yeah, that's... They played it way back though.
